---
title: "Circulatory disease deaths in Pennsylvania, 2018--2024"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
    theme: cosmo
    source_code: embed
runtime: shiny                                   # M2
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(shiny)                                   # M2
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# data: one row per county and year
raw <- read_tsv("data/pa_circulatory_deaths_2018_2024.txt",   # tab-separated
                col_types = cols(`County Code` = "c"))         # GEOID as text

pa <- raw |>
  filter(!is.na(Year)) |>                        # drop the "Total" rows
  mutate(GEOID      = `County Code`,
         county     = sub(" County, PA", "", County),          # "Lehigh", as in NAME
         year       = Year,
         cases      = Deaths,
         population = Population)

# boundaries
pa_map <- counties(state = "PA", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# M2: Pennsylvania by year reads no input, computed once
pa_year <- pa |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(population), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / pop, area = "Pennsylvania")

# M2: one set of classes for every period, from the pooled rates
pooled <- pa |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(rate = 1e5 * sum(cases) / sum(population), .groups = "drop")
breaks <- c(0, quantile(pooled$rate, c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8), na.rm = TRUE), Inf)
```

Column {.sidebar data-width=250}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r inputs}
# M2: the reader's choices
selectInput("county", "County",
            choices = sort(unique(pa$county)), selected = "Lehigh")

sliderInput("years", "Years",
            min = min(pa$year), max = max(pa$year),
            value = range(pa$year), step = 1, sep = "")   # sep: 2018, not 2,018
```

Pick a county, then drag either end of the slider. The map, the time
series and the table follow.

```{r reactive}
# M2: rate by county, for the selected years
by_county <- reactive({
  pa |>
    filter(between(year, input$years[1], input$years[2])) |>
    group_by(GEOID, county) |>
    summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(population), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / pop)             # per 100,000 person-years
})
```

Column {data-width=550}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Circulatory disease death rate by county, selected years (black outline: selected county)

```{r map}
renderLeaflet({                                  # M2
  d <- left_join(pa_map, by_county(), by = "GEOID")    # M2: join inside
  pal <- colorBin("YlOrRd", domain = d$rate, bins = breaks)

  leaflet(d) |>
    addProviderTiles(
      providers$Esri.WorldImagery,
      options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.5)
    ) |>
    addPolygons(
      fillColor = ~pal(rate), fillOpacity = 0.8,
      color = "white", weight = 1,
      label = ~sprintf("%s: %.1f per 100,000 (%.0f deaths)",
                       NAME, rate, cases),
      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                          bringToFront = TRUE)
    ) |>
    addPolygons(data = filter(d, NAME == input$county),   # M2: outline
                fill = FALSE, color = "black", weight = 3) |>
    addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~rate,
              title = paste0("Rate per 100,000<br>", input$years[1], "-", input$years[2]),
              labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 0), opacity = 0.8)
})
```

> Rate = deaths / population over the selected years, per 100,000 residents per year. Darker red: more circulatory disease deaths per resident. The classes are the quintiles of the 2018--2024 rates and stay the same for every period.

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Death rate by year, Pennsylvania and selected county (grey band: selected years)

```{r timeseries}
renderPlotly({                                   # M2
  one <- pa |>
    filter(county == input$county) |>            # M2: was focus
    mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / population, area = input$county)

  cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Pennsylvania", input$county))

  p <- ggplot(bind_rows(pa_year, one), aes(year, rate, colour = area)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = input$years[1] - 0.5,
             xmax = input$years[2] + 0.5,
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey90") +  # M2: selected years
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Rate per 100,000", colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal()

  ggplotly(p)                                    # hover, zoom
})
```

> Black: Pennsylvania; red: the selected county. Small counties have few deaths per year, so their line jumps more from year to year.

Column {.tabset data-width=350}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Counties, selected years

```{r table}
renderDT({                                       # M2
  by_county() |>
    transmute(County = county, Deaths = cases,
              Population = pop, Rate = round(rate, 1)) |>
    arrange(desc(Rate)) |>
    datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10)) |>
    formatStyle("County", target = "row",
                fontWeight = styleEqual(input$county, "bold"))  # M2: bold row
})
```

> Population is summed over the selected years (person-years). The selected county is in bold.

### About these data

- **Outcome:** deaths from diseases of the circulatory system (ICD-10 I00--I99), 2018--2024, by year.
- **Population at risk:** residents of Pennsylvania's 67 counties (Census Bureau estimates, via CDC WONDER).
- **Rate:** crude death rate, deaths / population x 100,000; on the map and in the table, deaths summed over the selected years divided by the population summed over the same years (person-years), an average annual rate.
- **Source:** [CDC WONDER, Multiple Cause of Death, 2018--2024, Single Race](https://wonder.cdc.gov/mcd.html); boundaries from the US Census Bureau, via `tigris`.
- **Areas without data:** none; no counts are suppressed.
- **Your choices:** the reader picks the county and the years in the sidebar; the map, the time series and the table follow.
- **Limitation:** the rates are crude, not age-adjusted, so counties with older populations (such as Cameron) look worse partly because of their age structure.
